# Technique — sound effects (frame-table SFX)

**Source:** standard frame-table SFX pattern; hardware basis `litmus_audio` (AUDC/AUDF/AUDV), tables generated by `pkg/audio` helpers.

**Goal:** the standard game SFX vocabulary as **data**: each effect is a frame table
(2 bytes/frame: `AUDC<<4|AUDV`, `AUDF`) generated by `pkg/audio` helpers, played by a tiny
per-frame tick. Effects are numerically verifiable (exact register sequence per frame).

Demo: `roms/techniques/sfx_demo.asm` (fire cycles through 5 effects).
CI: `scenarios/sfx_demo.json` (14 register asserts across all 5 effects + audio golden).
Generators: `pkg/audio` `PitchSweep` / `NoiseBurst` / `Blip` / `Arpeggio` / `EmitSFX` (unit-tested).

## The five standard recipes

| effect | generator | character |
|---|---|---|
| laser | `PitchSweep(4, 4, 22, 12, 12)` | square, descending sweep |
| explosion | `NoiseBurst(8, 6, 15, 24)` | white noise, linear decay to 0 |
| pickup | `Arpeggio(4, []int{19,14,11}, 4, 10)` | rising 3-note arpeggio (≈G5→C6→E6) |
| bounce | `Blip(6, 10, 10, 4)` | short low blip |
| engine | `NoiseBurst(3, 28, 8, 30)` | low rumble, slow decay |

## The player (12 lines of 6502, runs in overscan)

State: `sfxOn` / `sfxIdx` / `sfxLen` / table pointer (zp). Per frame, if active:

```
ldy sfxIdx
lda (ptr),y        ; AUDC<<4 | AUDV
sta tmp / and #$0F / sta AUDV0
lda tmp / lsr ×4   / sta AUDC0
iny / lda (ptr),y  / sta AUDF0
iny / sty sfxIdx
cpy sfxLen → done? AUDV0=0, sfxOn=0
```

Triggering = set pointer + length + `sfxOn=1` (the demo edge-detects INPT4 D7; a game calls the
same from its event code). One channel is enough for SFX; pair with the music driver
(`sound-driver.md`) for music + SFX priority.

## Why frame tables (and not code per effect)
- **Verifiable**: the scenario asserts the exact AUDC/AUDF/AUDV at chosen frames — confirmed all
  5 recipes register-exact on first run, plus a chained audio-digest golden.
- **Composable**: new effects are one `EmitSFX(...)` call away; tables live in ROM data.
- **Cheap**: tick ≈ 40 cycles in overscan; 2 bytes × duration per effect in ROM.

## Variations reported elsewhere (not in the demo)

None of these is generated by `pkg/audio` or played by `sfx_demo`, and none of them was built or
measured here. The one measurement named below belongs to `pitch-dither.md`; the arpeggio item
cites it for comparison, and it does not cover the arpeggio itself.

- **Two timbres alternating every frame (Space Chase explosion).** Karl G, on the explosion in
  Apollo's *Space Chase*: *"it's 45 frames long, with the volume starting at max and decrementing
  every 3 frames. AUDC and AUDF alternate every other frame between AUDC=2, AUDF=7 and AUDC=3,
  AUDF=10"* 〔AtariAge `topic/267305`, 2017〕. One voice, two (AUDC, AUDF) pairs swapped frame by
  frame; unlike the AUDF-only swap in `pitch-dither.md`, AUDC changes too. The 2-byte table above
  can hold it as it is (the player writes AUDC every frame); no `pkg/audio` generator emits it.
  **Cited only, not verified.**
- **A quiet tail on explosions.** Thomas Jentzsch, on the explosions in Manuel Rotschkar's
  *Seawolf* alpha: *"IMO the volume is reduced too rapidly when getting low. Usually explosions
  have some low volume echoes at the end."* 〔stella-list `200403/msg00195`〕; in his first reply he
  had called them *"a bit too short"* and suggested fading them *"a bit slower or maybe make some
  double explosion sounds"* 〔`200403/msg00191`〕. Manuel answered that for now they were *"synced to
  the animation length"* 〔`200403/msg00196`〕; after Paul Slocum also asked whether he had
  considered an echo effect 〔`200403/msg00197`〕, he wrote he would *"really try to achieve echoed
  effects"* 〔`200403/msg00199`〕. No result is posted in the thread, and this is a listening opinion,
  not a measurement. The `explosion` recipe above (`NoiseBurst`, linear decay to 0) has no such
  tail. **Cited only, not verified.**
- **Effect state in one byte (a suggestion).** For Erik Eid's *Euchre*, zu03776 wrote: *"If you
  have a byte of RAM left, you could program a sound subroutine to call every frame, and the value
  of the byte to determine what effect to play. The upper three bits could determine effect, and
  lower five bits for number of frames (left) to play effect."* … *"That's five effects (counting
  silence) -- or if the frame count is zero, then play silence."* 〔stella-list `200207/msg00305`〕
  Three bits name up to 8 effects and five bits count up to 31 frames (our arithmetic); compare the
  four zp variables of the player above. Paul Slocum answered that *"Probably the sound effects
  could be done without using any extra RAM by just adding sound into the routines that handle the
  game logic"*, as he had done in *Marble Craze*, using *Euchre*'s existing status variables and
  delay counter to time them 〔`200207/msg00306`〕. Erik Eid replied he was *"not all that short on
  RAM"* (ROM was his concern) and might borrow a song routine from Bob Colbert's *Okie Dokie*
  instead 〔`200207/msg00309`〕; both replies are also quoted in `audio-envelope-idioms.md`. A
  proposal, not a reported build. **Cited only, not verified.**
- **A hold count per row; a 0 in every played channel stops playback (Eckhard Stolberg's editor
  format).** His 1997 Supercharger
  sound editor shows each line as `VCPPFF` in hex: V goes to AUDV, C to AUDC, PP to AUDF, and FF
  *"is the number of frames (60 per second), that the other values in that line should stay in the
  registers, before it advances to the next line"*; *"The playback stops, if a line, with the
  number of frames set to 0, has occured in all played channels"* 〔stella-list `199706/msg00049`〕.
  Asked about sweeps, he answered that a 1-frame duration per line allows a different volume in
  every line, but with 256 lines per channel *"that's not really enough to do long songs with
  complicated volume envelopes"*, and that for such effects *"writing a special program and
  changing the calculation routine everytime might be easier"* 〔`199707/msg00014`〕. Against the
  table above (one row per frame, length in `sfxLen`), a held row saves bytes on steady stretches
  at the cost of a per-row frame counter, and the 0 row replaces the length (our reading).
  **Cited only, not verified.**
- **How fast an arpeggio can step.** Paul Slocum's 2003 music guide, on chord arpeggios:
  *"Typically I do a note per step in my music driver. I have tried running arpeggios at a note per
  frame (60 per second) but it sounds bad when it gets that fast. You introduce 60Hz noise at that
  speed."* 〔stella-list `200302/msg00208`〕 The same guide says that for most songs a step is
  *"3/60ths to 4/60ths of a second"*; the `pickup` recipe's 4 frames per note is at the long end
  of that range. `pitch-dither.md` does recommend a per-frame swap, and it also measured that swap
  as adding almost no energy outside a fifth either side of the note (within 1.3× of the steady
  tone on all four notes; `TestTheDitherAddsNoRoughness`), but only between two adjacent AUDF rungs
  standing for one pitch, not across an arpeggio's wide steps. **Cited only, not verified.**
- **Both channels, two waveforms, one fade (deep explosion).** A 2007 AtariAge recipe sets both
  channels to AUDF 31 at the same volume, AUDC 15 on channel 0 and AUDC 8 on channel 1, and lowers
  that shared volume by one each frame 〔AtariAge `topic/112016`; read from our notes, the thread
  text is not kept here〕. Unlike the one-channel recipes above, it takes both voices while it
  plays. **Cited only, not verified.**
